title: Rabbi Yehudah the Baker
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He lived in Rabbi Akiva’s generation, as Hyman argues from Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:5: “Rabbi Yehudah the Baker said (in Rosh Hashanah 22a it reads Rabbi Yehudah without further designation): Heaven forbid! Rabbi Akiva was not excommunicated; rather, the head of Gader was, and Rabban Gamliel sent and removed him from his headship.” In Bava Batra 132a: “Rabbi Yehudah the Baker said: An incident with my sister’s daughter, a bride,” etc. (The Rashbam explains that his son married his sister’s daughter.) He is likewise mentioned in Menachot 6b: “Rabbi Yose ben Yose ben Yasyan and Rabbi Yehudah the Baker said: When is this said? When he took the handful,” etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah, beginning of chapter 2, and Kohelet Rabbah 7:8 [it is related] that he was one of those executed by the government, and Elisha ben Avuyah saw his tongue in a dog’s mouth and said: “This is Torah, and this is its reward?”
He is likewise mentioned in Eichah Rabbah, chapter 2, on “He swallowed,” and Midrash Tehillim 9:13: Ben Kufya wished to save him, and it was decreed that he too be killed.

notes.text: Saved Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah1:5 explicitly says Akiva was not excommunicated, matching Hyman’s received sense; נחנדה is read as נתנדה. Saved Davidson Bavli22a instead says Akiva did not detain the witnesses. These edition-specific accounts are not silently conflated. חו״ש and שכרהה are read as חס ושלום and שכרה.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:5 explicitly names Yehudah the Baker and says Rabbi Akiva was not excommunicated. The consulted Bavli 22a instead says Akiva did not detain the witnesses. These distinct accounts remain distinct; the Bavli’s unqualified Yehudah is not silently used to establish the heading’s identity.
